title: Resiliency check & handoff notes — Aug 26 2026
content:
TL;DR:
- Quiet weekend overall but two small-to-medium incidents touched tokenization and cache layers. No SLO breaches, error budget for the month down to ~18%.
- On-call transition Wednesday -> Thursday observed gaps in escalation matrix for 3rd-party cache provider. Action item assigned.
- This doc captures the handoff log, incident notes, short SLO snapshot, and immediate action items. Add to weekly SRE sync on Friday for prioritization.

Highlights and context:
- Goal this week: verify resilience of fast-path cache + tokenization microservice under tail load and validate alert thresholds after rolling kernel upgrade on prom nodes.
- Recent infra change: kernel and nvidia-driver roll completed on 2026-08-24 for us-west-2 inference pool. No regression in throughput observed, but noticed increased KV cache eviction rates for long-context sessions.

Incident summaries (concise):
1) INC-2026-344 — embeddings-cache thrash (2026-08-25 02:47–03:15 UTC)
   - Symptom: Elevated 5xx rate (up to 1.6% from baseline 0.02%) for the embeddings cache tier leading to higher tail latency on embedding lookups.
   - Root cause hypothesis: Combined effect of kernel page reclaim behavior + increased long-lived key churn after a customer load test. Third-party in-memory store reported transient GC spikes.
   - Mitigation steps taken: throttled background cache refill, temporarily bumped retries in client to reduce hot-looping, scaled read replicas by +2 in us-east-1 and us-west-2.
   - Outcome: error rate back to baseline within 28 minutes. No SLO breach. Follow-ups: deeper GC tracing on cache nodes and add a circuit-breaker for refill storms.

2) TOKEN-03 — tokenization service CPU spin (2026-08-26 10:12–10:42 UTC)
   - Symptom: Tokenization microservice (tokenizer-v2) experienced CPU starve on a subset of pods after a sudden spike of short-latency requests (spike from 120 rps to 2.1k rps). P95 latency hit 420ms (baseline 18ms).
   - Mitigation: emergency autoscale policy triggered; increased pod replicas, applied a temporary rate-limit on unauthenticated routes, and routed high-cost requests to a lower-priority queue.
   - Root cause: autoscaler config used CPU util thresholds unsuitable for short bursty bursts (scale-up lag). Also client-side retry loops amplified the spike.
   - Outcome: tail latency recovered after 20 minutes. Action items: adjust autoscaler cooldown, implement request shaping at edge, provide client guidance on sensible retry/backoff.

SLO snapshot (weekly):
- User-facing text generation availability SLO: 99.95% (rolling 30d). Current rolling-period: 99.963% — error budget remaining ~18% for the month.
- Tokenization P95 target: 40ms. Current 30d rolling P95: 36ms. Last 7 days P95 spiked to 58ms during tokenization incident window.
- Embeddings store error-rate target: <0.5% per region. Observed spike to 1.6% during incident, now back to 0.03% baseline.
- Remaining action: re-evaluate alert thresholds after we finish GC tracing and replay long-session churn tests.

On-call handoff log (chronological):
- Outgoing: Ethan Liu (shift end 2026-08-26 08:00 UTC)
  - Notes left: watch INC-2026-344 follow-up, PR #742 to runtime (queued), throttle rules for cache refill updated in helm chart staging.
- Incoming: Marta Rodriguez (start 2026-08-26 08:00 UTC)
  - Acknowledged active watches and will run the scheduled tail-load simulation @ noon.
- Mid-shift escalation: Omar Khan paged in for tokenization spike; led mitigation and performed runbook steps.
- Handoff checklist completed by incoming: yes (confirmed), additional items: confirm ES-based alerting for kernel page reclaim metrics.

Runbook & playbook notes:
- Short-term: add a 'burst-safe' autoscaler profile for tokenization (lower CPU threshold + faster scale-up steps).
- Cache: implement refill circuit-breaker and backpressure signal from cache client. Add a synthetic that mimics long-context churn and run every 6 hours against staging.
- Observability: add flame/CPU profiles during refill windows, enable jemalloc stats on cache nodes for next deploy.

Open action items (owners & ETA):
- SRE-512 (Omar) — GC tracing on cache nodes + report (ETA 2026-09-02)
- SRE-519 (Priya) — Update autoscaler policies and add burst profile to k8s HPA (ETA 2026-08-29)
- SRE-523 (Zoe) — Edge request shaping prototype and client retry guidance doc (ETA 2026-09-06)
- Ops-tiling (Marta) — Schedule 6-hour churn synthetic against staging and post results (ETA 2026-08-28)

Risks and notes for leadership:
- Risk: repeated long-session churn from a single enterprise tenant could erode embeddings error budget quickly. Recommend engaging account team for coordinated load-window if we need to run capacity tests that mimic production.
- Note: kernel/driver upgrades are low risk but observability gaps on memory reclaim metrics need filling before next upgrade window.

Meeting asks for Friday SRE sync:
- Prioritize autoscaler burst profile vs circuit-breaker for cache refill (vote + pros/cons).
- Review of SRE-512 GC tracing results and proposed permanent alert thresholds.
- Decide whether to enable jemalloc stats on prod cache nodes (security vs observability tradeoff).

Appendix (short links & references):
- Incident ticket: INC-2026-344
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-512, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-519
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/742
- Playbook: confluence:Resiliency-Playbook-v2

Note to reviewers: this is a working handoff doc. Please add comments inline or tag @Priya for clarifications. If urgent, page in the #sre-oncall channel.
